messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 SEV-2 alert: continuous-batching throughput-drop detected on shard rwd-prod-eu-3. Queue depth spiked +420% in last 60s. Related signals: KV cache miss rate up, microbatch size oscillation, tail latency > 2s for 95th pct. Pager triggered for on-call.

sam (on-call): on it. seeing a sudden ramp in inflight requests to the cb pool, lots of small microbatches. attaching recent metrics. :eyes:

anya: I can pull logs and the KV eviction telemetry. preliminary looks like a K/V cache thrash — eviction rate soared around 1779998820.

kai: do we have customer-facing errors? any 5xx spikes?

sam (on-call): some clients seeing elevated 503/504 when requests time out on the queue. not widespread but high-value tenants in eu-west impacted. outage window ~ 1779998780-1779999060 so far.

lucas: sending a quick heatmap of microbatch sizes — lots of jitter causing many tiny batches then sudden big ones. continuous batching scheduler seems to be oscillating.

marie: hypothesis: under high concurrency the batching heuristic falls back causing suboptimal batch composition and KV cache churn. two-pronged mitigation: 1) clamp microbatch min-size to reduce jitter, 2) temporarily increase KV cache headroom / lower eviction aggressiveness.

sam (on-call): agree. I can apply a runtime knob for min_microbatch = 8 on the eu shard and nuke aggressive eviction flag. prepping a runbook step.

anya: logs show repeated cache rehydration RPCs to s3 for hot prefixes — that explains latency spike. if we reduce evictions we'll reduce rehydration and lower latency.

kai: are there any config risks for increasing cache headroom? memory pressure on node level?

lucas: nodes currently at 72% mem. bumping headroom by 15% should be safe short term. will watch OOM.

sam (on-call): executing step 1: setting min_microbatch=8 on rwd-prod-eu-3 now.

deploy-bot: deploy request #D-4821 initiated by sam. rolling to rwd-prod-eu-3 config: {"min_microbatch":8} . ETA ~ 30s.

sam (on-call): step 2 queued: toggle cache_eviction.mode -> "grace" (less aggressive). will wait for microbatch change to stabilize for 2 min then flip.

anya: microbatch distribution stabilizing in the graphs. jitter is down. queue depth decreasing. latency 95p trending toward normal. :thumbsup:

marie: proceeding to flip eviction mode in 30s. will monitor eviction rate and rehydration RPCs.

deploy-bot: config change applied: cache_eviction.mode -> "grace" on rwd-prod-eu-3.

lucas: eviction rate dropped 78% vs peak. KV rehydration calls to s3 are down. tail latency 95p now ~450ms (was >2s).

sam (on-call): stabilizing. I’m going to rate-limit a small noisy tenant for temporary relief — doing a soft throttle on team-internal test keys (10rps).

kai: noted. Can we roll a quick microbatch scheduling patch to reduce future oscillation? might be safer than manual knobs.

marie: I have a patch branch that reduces scheduler dampening and folds in a moving-average of batch arrival times. can cut a hotfix but prefer to run the config knobs for short-term.

anya: customer impact summary for ops: affected customers: subset of EU-hosted tenants (estimated 12/2000), some saw increased error rates and higher tail latency for ~5-6 minutes. No data loss.

sam (on-call): incident status: mitigation applied (min_microbatch clamp + relaxed eviction). system stabilized by 1779999060. keeping channel open for 30m for post-mortem artifacts.

lucas: capturing telemetry dump and will post graphs to the incident doc. planning a follow-up PR for scheduler hotfix and an automated guard to clamp KV eviction under high miss-rate.

marie: action items: 1) ship scheduler dampening PR (kai + lucas) 2) add an automated circuit to reduce eviction aggressiveness when rehydration RTT > 200ms (anya) 3) add customer-facing note and internal RCA (sam)

sam (on-call): handing off to oncall+shift lead for follow-up. handing to kai in 10m for next watch.

kai: taking handoff. leaving escalation phone number in the incident doc. good job team. :raised_hands:
